summary: Establishes a monthly universal child assistance payment to every U.S. child under 19 equal to one-twelfth the gap between HHS poverty guidelines for a two-person household and a single person, administered by a new SSA office using IRS data, while terminating the child tax credit and EITC after 2025 and creating new refundable credits of $700 per adult dependent and $700–$1,400 for adults and families with income phaseouts.

scores.thoughts: The bill establishes a new universal child assistance program administered by the SSA, providing monthly payments to all qualifying children under 19. This constitutes a major expansion of direct federal spending. It terminates the CTC and EITC but replaces them with new refundable credits and a direct payment system, resulting in net expansion of government outlays. Strongly pushes toward expanded spending.

The bill terminates the Child Tax Credit and Earned Income Tax Credit after 2025. It introduces two new refundable credits (adult dependent credit and credit for adults/families) with phaseouts. While it eliminates two credits, the overall structure maintains or expands tax-based transfers rather than broadly lowering taxes. Minor net effect toward higher effective transfers via tax code.
The bill has no provisions related to healthcare coverage, insurance markets, Medicaid, Medicare, or any health policy. No bearing on the topic.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues. No bearing on the topic.

The bill defines qualifying children to include U.S. citizens, nationals, and qualified aliens (per PRWORA). It uses IRS data sharing for eligibility but does not expand or restrict immigration pathways, visas, or border policy. Tangential at most.
No provisions related to abortion access, funding, restrictions, or reproductive health. No bearing on the topic.
No provisions address military, defense spending, or national security appropriations. No bearing on the topic.
No provisions related to environmental regulations, climate policy, energy, or conservation. No bearing on the topic.

The core of the bill is a new universal monthly child assistance payment program, explicitly designed to end child poverty, with payments disregarded as income for other federal programs. This directly expands the social safety net with a new universal benefit. Strongly pushes toward expansion.
No provisions address schools, school choice, federal education funding, or privatization. No bearing on the topic.
No provisions related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance abuse programs. No bearing on the topic.
No provisions address policing, sentencing, rehabilitation, or criminal justice reform. No bearing on the topic.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization. No bearing on the topic.

The bill creates a large new entitlement-style spending program without any offsetting revenue increases or spending cuts elsewhere, implying increased deficit spending. Pushes toward accepting deficit spending.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections, nondiscrimination, or related issues. No bearing on the topic.
No provisions address foreign aid, international assistance, or State Department funding. No bearing on the topic.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, voter ID, or electoral reform. No bearing on the topic.
The bill includes IRS data sharing with SSA for eligibility determination but contains no broader tech regulation, data privacy rules, or platform oversight. Tangential at most.
No provisions address union rights, worker protections, collective bargaining, or employer flexibility. No bearing on the topic.
No provisions address religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or conflicts between religious liberty and antidiscrimination laws. No bearing on the topic.

The bill creates a new universal child assistance entitlement program with monthly payments to all qualifying children under 19, calculated from federal poverty guidelines, administered by a new SSA office. It terminates the CTC and EITC but replaces them with two new refundable credits (adult dependent and adults/families), resulting in net new mandatory spending with no revenue offsets or cuts identified. This is the bill's core purpose, making deficit impact highly central.
